existing_event_updates.summary: Kpler preliminary data reported four commodity-vessel transits Thursday, three inbound and one outbound, down from six Wednesday and below a ten-day average near 16. AIS-off traffic remains an explicit undercount limitation; Bab el-Mandeb recorded 23 versus a ten-day average near 26.

Reuters satellite analysis and three industry sources independently confirmed damage at three pumping stations. The 1,200-km pipeline temporarily shut; three sources estimated five-to-six-week repairs while another allowed earlier partial pumping. Station damage is confirmed; destruction of the pipeline body is not.

Iranian state media named the Togo-flagged tanker as Trend and attributed the statement to IRGC Navy commander Rear Adm. Ali Azmaei. Vessel naming remains claimant-source at this horizon; weapon, casualties, independent damage confirmation and claimed U.S. involvement remain unresolved.

Reuters aid-agency reporting placed about 115,000 people on the move while AP cited OCHA around 125,000 and separate casualty figures. These series use different denominators/cutoffs and must not overwrite or be arithmetically merged with IOM DTM.

AP separately reported Oman hosted a weekend U.S.-Houthi meeting, strengthening existence of the direct channel. Public evidence still did not establish a formal new nonaggression agreement or exact terms.

Reuters reported Iran would be on the Sep.24 Trump-Xi summit agenda and Treasury planned discussion of China's financial ties to Tehran. This extends the pressure track but does not establish a Chinese commitment to coerce Iran.

claims_and_corrections.claim: Trend attempted an unauthorized Hormuz passage at U.S. military direction and was struck, set ablaze and stopped.
claims_and_corrections.summary: Preserve vessel identity, physical-effect and U.S.-direction propositions separately; claimant-source naming does not independently establish all propositions.

economic_energy_updates.summary: Brent and WTI remained above $100. Reuters relayed a secondary report that at least two European customers were told they would receive no October Saudi crude; preserve customer-allocation reporting as secondary until supplier/customer confirmation.
